sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct used as functional WT backbone for variant studies; explicit surface-expression or enzymatic-activity assay of the tagged WT not described in the clip.
sites.rationale: MEP1B is a type I transmembrane protein (signal peptide 1–22, extracellular 23–652, TM 653–675, intracellular 676–701). An 'N-terminal' tag on a full-length construct with a signal peptide must be inserted after the SP cleavage site (after residue 22) to survive to the cell surface; placement upstream of residue 1 would be cleaved off with the signal peptide. The junction is therefore uniquely determined by topology: insert_after_residue = 22, placing the strep tag at the mature extracellular N-terminus, 630 residues from the TM boundary. Python confirmed residue 22 = A and residue 23 = T. Full-length meprin β WT pcDNA4/to construct carrying an N-terminal strep tag and a C-terminal flag tag, used as the backbone for generating the R238Q variant; expressed in a mammalian system.

sources.claim: A plasmid coding for the meprin β variant R238Q was generated on the basis of a meprin β WT pcDNA4/to-construct that carries an N-terminal strep tag and a C-terminal flag tag.

literature_notes: L1, L2, and L3 all describe a C-terminally HA-tagged murine meprin β expressed from a Rosa26 knock-in. MEP1B is a type I TM protein whose C-terminus (residues 676–701) is intracellular; the HA tag therefore faces the cytoplasm and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. These are recorded in other_positions. L4 describes a doubly-tagged construct (N-terminal strep + C-terminal flag); the C-terminal flag is likewise intracellular and is also recorded in other_positions. Only the N-terminal strep tag of L4 lands on the extracellular face and is reported as a site. No ledger line names a specific residue for the N-terminal junction, so position_evidence is topology_derived. No internal extracellular loop insertions are supported by any ledger line.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag on murine meprin β (Rosa26 knock-in); the C-terminus (residues 676–701) is intracellular, so the HA tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
C-terminal flag tag on full-length meprin β pcDNA4/to construct; same intracellular C-terminus (676–701), not accessible from the extracellular face.
